notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in it counts as correct for this topic_id.

This is a SECOND, independent synthetic application (Continental Imaging Decommission Services, Inc.) against the same true_requirements.json as data/36C25926Q0699 -- built to add SFT/eval training data with deliberately different failure and compliance shapes from the original application (Summit Biomedical Field Services, LLC).

Error-shape diversity versus the original: rfq_completeness_signature is now an explicit missing-date gap rather than an ambiguous compliant/insufficient case; personnel_qualifications_fse is now a clean quantitative shortfall (18 months stated) rather than a claimed-vs-actual-tenure contradiction, since that contradiction shape is already the canonical example for this exact topic in the original application; gwac_mas_pricing_disclosure, deliverables_field_service_report, safety_ppe_bloodborne_pathogens, and past_performance_questionnaire_ppq are inverted to compliant rather than the original's non_compliant/insufficient; subcontractor_disclosure_statement is a new contradiction (a named subcontractor mentioned mid-document versus a closing 'no subcontractors' statement) not exercised in the original.
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone.

primary_verdict / primary_verdict_source (added by SFT data-prep pass): a single training-target label per topic, additive -- acceptable_verdicts is unchanged and remains the source of truth for verdict-accuracy scoring. primary_verdict is the pipeline's own correct prediction where one exists (source: pipeline_prediction), else acceptable_verdicts[0] (source: acceptable_verdicts_first). null for topics with acceptable_verdicts: null (excluded from SFT training, same as they're excluded from verdict scoring).

verdicts.rationale: Application is signed with a printed name and signature block but no date appears anywhere in the document -- an explicit, unambiguous gap in the signed-and-dated requirement.

verdicts.description: Volume I must demonstrate how the offeror's quote meets the Statement of Work and solicitation requirements, including testing plans, lab certifications, and alignment with the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP).
verdicts.rationale: Volume I addresses the Statement of Work requirements section by section (contract vehicle, infection control, floor area, reporting, personnel, safety).

verdicts.description: The technical approach must establish and maintain an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) Level IV compliant work area around the Radiology room -- dust barriers and protective measures as directed by facility Infection Prevention/Safety staff, plus debris control, cleaning, and containment throughout the work.
verdicts.rationale: Application describes an ICRA Level IV compliant work area with dust barriers and continuous debris control, cleaning, and containment.

verdicts.description: The technical approach must address removing anchoring bolts/hardware from the floor, restoring the floor to a flush condition suitable for future construction, and removing all resulting trash and debris.
verdicts.rationale: Application addresses removing anchoring bolts/hardware and removing resulting trash and debris, but never confirms the floor is restored to a flush condition suitable for future construction -- one of the three required elements is unaddressed.

evidence.quote:
Continental will remove all anchoring
bolts and other hardware associated with the GE INNOVA 4100-IQ installation from the

verdicts.description: The offeror's approach must account for delivering a detailed field service report upon completion, at minimum covering equipment identification, dates/times on site, description of tasks performed, confirmation of the monitor arm's final disposition, and any issues encountered with corrective actions taken.
verdicts.rationale: Application's field service report description covers equipment identification, dates/times on site, task description, monitor arm disposition, and issues/corrective actions -- all five required elements.

evidence.quote:

service report to Biomedical Engineering and the COR identifying the equipment removed

verdicts.rationale: Application explicitly states the lead Field Service Engineer has only 18 months of field experience, short of the 2-year minimum the requirement sets.

verdicts.description: The contractor's approach must comply with the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard: educating employees on risks, implementing exposure-reduction policies/procedures, providing counseling/treatment mechanisms after potential exposure, and providing/enforcing PPE use.
verdicts.rationale: Application addresses all four required Bloodborne Pathogens Standard elements: employee education on risks, exposure-reduction procedures, post-exposure counseling/treatment referral, and PPE enforcement.

verdicts.description: Offeror must list any/all subcontractors it will use (with their size standard under NAICS 541380) and what they will perform, and explain how it will comply with the limitations on subcontracting -- or state that no subcontractors will be used.
verdicts.rationale: Application states in the Past Performance section that a named subcontractor (Redline Environmental Services) will handle debris disposal, but the closing line of the quote states no subcontractors will be used -- the two statements directly conflict.

verdicts.description: By certifying compliance with the VAAR 852.219-75 clause for this services acquisition, the offeror represents it will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the Government to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs/VOSBs.
